migrationBoundary.reason: These authority-complete rules require literal king-capture moves that standard-chess/v1 never generates. They remain outside the frozen v2 model vocabulary until an authority-aware v3 corpus and model migration is released.

rules.name: Femme Fatale
rules.observedDescription: You can only capture their king with a queen
sourceEvidence: Chess.com community glossary compiled by Truc1231
ambiguities: Primary pre-move piece type controls: a pawn that promotes while capturing the king is not yet a queen and is rejected.
The source does not separately describe the authority's castling-en-passant king-capture edge; it is treated as a king capture and therefore requires a queen primary mover.

rules.name: Nurturer
rules.observedDescription: You can't capture their king until you've promoted a pawn
sourceEvidence: Chess.com community glossary compiled by Truc1231
ambiguities: A promotion must complete before it unlocks king capture, so a capture-promotion of the king cannot satisfy its own prerequisite.
Promotion history is reconstructed from supplied affected-player move history; a preloaded promoted piece without complete history does not silently unlock the rule.
The unlock never resets if the promoted piece is later captured.

rules.name: Triple Play
rules.observedDescription: You can only capture their king if you have three (random piece)
sourceEvidence: Chess.com community glossary compiled by Truc1231
InvalidSE/DrawbackDetector pinned observation corpus: 7 observations; five knight and two bishop parameter texts
ambiguities: The generated domain is limited to bishop and knight because those are the only parameter values in the pinned source-site observations; no other piece type is inferred.
Have three is provisionally interpreted as at least three rather than exactly three.
Material is counted on the pre-move board and promoted pieces count by current type, so a capture-promotion cannot become the third required piece during the king-capture move.

rules.name: You Best Not Miss
rules.observedDescription: If you end your turn checking your opponent, you must capture their king on the next move (or lose)
sourceEvidence: Chess.com community glossary compiled by Truc1231
ambiguities: Every geometric attack on the present opponent king triggers the delayed obligation; the wording does not say the future capture must already be guaranteed.
Next move means the next affected-player turn after the opponent reply.
If the opponent removes every king-capture reply, the shared zero-filter adjudication produces a start-of-turn drawback loss.
Arbitrary midgame reconstruction requires persisted rule state because current FEN plus move history cannot prove whether the affected player's prior move gave check before the opponent replied.

rules.name: Irresistible
rules.observedDescription: If you can move a piece adjacent to your opponent's king that isn't already, you must, except that you are always permitted to capture their king
sourceEvidence: Chess.com community glossary compiled by Truc1231
InvalidSE/DrawbackDetector pinned observation corpus: 7 identical observations
ambiguities: Only a primary mover that was not adjacent before the move can satisfy the forced destination; moving an already-adjacent piece to another adjacent square does not trigger or satisfy the obligation.
Castling uses the primary king endpoints, promotion and en-passant use the primary pawn endpoints, and auxiliary rook or removed-pawn squares do not control adjacency.
Every literal authority-generated opposing-king capture remains legal even when one or more newly adjacent moves exist, including the one-reply castling-en-passant king-capture right.
